extends.new-data: Year 4 reports 231 systems and over 1.8 MW installed in 2023, bringing Solarize totals to 4.8 MW and 630+ households served.
The source adds specific Year 4 municipal solar deployments, nearly 4 MW of additional sites in design, and $2.5 million in federal support plus election center solar funding.
Year 4 says the Wheeler Center/former landfill solar effort was re-scoped and received a $5 million award to advance solar at and around the site.
The report says the city drafted CCA legislation and continued state-level advocacy alongside Michigan's new clean energy law package.
Year 4 adds a technical study, rate analysis, public engagement launch, and a planned November 2024 ballot question on formally creating the SEU.
The source provides 2023 fuel-mix context, notes over 50% coal and 13% renewables, and ties this to municipalization study and MPSC case interventions.
Year 4 expands resilience hub work with EPA funding for a regional network, new planned sites, and added backup power investments.
The report indicates Bryant Community Center became the city's second resilience hub, shifting the hub network from a single-site model to expansion.
Year 4 reports 8,903 trees planted or distributed, a USFS grant for canopy analysis and underserved-neighborhood planting, and a planned survival study.
The source adds an air-quality visualization map, reliability fixes, and six additional monitors ordered for deployment.
Year 4 reports the 5th and 6th cohorts, reaching 100 ambassadors trained, plus science communication training and neighborhood pilot work.
The report says the city reached 25% electrification of light-duty fleet vehicles, added e-bikes, and set a 70% fleet electrification Year 5 priority.
Year 4 adds the state's first curbside public L2 chargers, park-site charger expansion, a multifamily/commercial discount program, and a grant for two dozen more locations.
The source updates TheRide work with a zero-emissions propulsion study and grant application for its first zero-emission buses.
Year 4 adds Bryant district geothermal design details, a citywide networked geothermal study, and geothermal support at 121 Catherine Street.
The report says over $4 million was authorized for residential rebates over 2.5 years through a new Home Energy Rebate program design contract.
Year 4 says the Green Rental Housing program made significant progress and was expected to go to City Council in summer or fall 2024.
The source says the A2ZERO Home Energy Advisor service launched as a free resident-facing decarbonization guidance program.
Year 4 reports active implementation of the commercial and multifamily benchmarking ordinance for buildings over 20,000 square feet and launch of Home Energy Rating Disclosure.
The report expands circular economy work with ZeroWaste.Org contracting, planning toward a development strategy, GIS map updates, and the More Life Less Stuff campaign.

theme-connections: State clean-energy legislation reshapes local renewable, utility, and electrification pathways.
Bryant emerges as a flagship district linking geothermal, resilience, efficiency, and engagement.
City is shifting from pilots to delivery infrastructure through multi-year contracts, grants, and ballot measures.
Resilience investments increasingly pair backup power, microgrids, and community-serving facilities.
Building decarbonization now spans homeowner guidance, rebates, disclosure, benchmarking, and workforce development.
